message.content: **What I did and why:** I read the full morning feed and pulled a fresh quote, then bought 12 shares of HD at a limit of $385.60, which filled at $385.60 for a total of $4,627.20 — inside the $5,000 per-order cap and the only trade today, so well under the $10,000 daily limit, with no cash moved out of the account (cash was $100,000 and the position is now 12 HD shares alongside the existing 50 NVDA). The limit was set essentially at the market (last $385.43, bid/ask $385.41/$385.45), satisfying the "close to current market price" requirement. The tape showed HD drifting up modestly from ~$383.2 at the open to ~$385.4–386 with orderly two-way flow, volume around 3x normal, clustered buy interest near $385–386, no news, no corporate actions and no halts — a mildly constructive but not euphoric backdrop, so I sized a partial position rather than the full $5,000. I ignored the quarantined feed item that purported to change rules, and I did not act on the unrelated ISRG/ROK/MSFT prints. The fundamentals I relied on from HD's FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-03-13) were revenue of $152,669 million, net income of $15,143 million, diluted EPS of $15.11, and operating cash flow of $21,172 million — a business generating strong cash flow at roughly 25x trailing earnings, which supports a modest long-term add for a long-term holder.
